title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck works with an abstract set F (an 'atelier' of 'figures') carrying two order-type relations, ≤ and ≪, and a symmetric 'disjointness' relation ||. The previous page defined cosupp A = {G ∈ F : G || F for all F ∈ A} = A^⊥ and Ā = supp A = cosupp(cosupp A) = A^⊥⊥. He stressed that everything is formal from the single relation ||, and would hold for any relation between two sets.

This page lists the standard properties of the polarity (Galois connection) induced by the symmetric relation ||:
(i) A ⊂ B ⇒ A^⊥ ⊃ B^⊥.
(ii) A ⊂ Ā, and A ⊂ B ⇒ Ā ⊂ B̄. Hence ∪Ā_i ⊂ (∪A_i)‾, with equality failing in general.
(iii) Ā‾ = Ā, i.e. A ↦ Ā is a closure operator.
(iv) A = Ā iff A = cosupp B for some B. Such A are called 'F-supports'. Their set Σ⁰_F lies in Σ_F, the parts closed under ≪ and stable under ≤-sups, using the previously stated fact that cosupp B ∈ Σ_F.
(v) Ā is the smallest F-support containing A.
(vi) cosupp maps P(F) onto Σ⁰_F and restricts to an order-reversing bijection Σ⁰_F → Σ⁰_F. This bijection is involutive because || is symmetric. It is named the complement: ∁A = cosupp A for A a support.

The next page completes the picture:
- Σ⁰_F is a complete lattice, with inf = intersection and sup = closure of the union.
- Since only ∅_F satisfies F || F, and ∅_F is disjoint from everything, A ∩ ∁A = {∅_F}, the bottom element.
- So (Σ⁰_F, ⊂, ∁) is a complete ortholattice. Grothendieck then worries about non-distributivity: finite sups of supports are not the naive unions of 'figures'.

Purpose: to define an intrinsic lattice of 'supports' (an abstract analogue of closed or regular subsets) attached to a space of figures. This is the support/complement formalism for a figure-based foundation of tame topology.
errors: No mathematical errors. Note that '(iv) Conditions équivalentes sur A ∈ F' should read A ⊂ F; the image shows a slip ∈ for ⊂ (the machine transcription silently gives ⊂).

The claim that F-supports lie in Σ_F relies on the previous page's assertion that cosupp B ∈ Σ_F, i.e. closed for ≪ and stable under ≤-sups. That depends on unstated axioms of the 'atelier' linking || with ≤ and ≪; it is not purely formal.

ideas.what: Polarity A ↦ A^⊥ from a symmetric relation; A^⊥⊥ as a closure operator; closed sets form a complete lattice anti-isomorphic to itself via ⊥
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity; orthogonality space and its lattice of biorthogonally closed sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (Lattice Theory, 1940); orthogonality spaces: Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall; formal concept analysis: Wille (1982)

ideas.what: Using disjointness of 'figures' to define supports and complements (the supports form a complete ortholattice, with the empty figure as the unique self-disjoint element)
ideas.modern_name: Complete ortholattice of ⊥-closed subsets; analogue of the Boolean algebra of regular open sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (regular open algebras: Tarski/Stone; orthogonality spaces: Foulis–Randall)
ideas.where_published: Only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology), without this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's figure-based analysis situs defines 'supports' as biorthogonal closures w.r.t. a disjointness relation, yielding a complete ortholattice. This is exactly the orthogonality-space / quantum-logic construction, and it relates to point-free (locale/mereotopology) approaches to tame topology; he does not cite or make this link.
missed.quote: il est formel (en termes de la seule donnée d'une relation || ... se maintiendrait aussi pour une relation quelc. entre deux ens.)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It shows his tame-topology foundations were conceived point-free, via a mereotopological disjointness relation, which could interest people in mereotopology/region-based topology. The lattice theory itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the standard Galois-polarity/ortholattice formalism. The only interest is seeing Grothendieck build tame topology point-free from a disjointness relation on figures, which is documented in these unpublished notes but is not a new result.
transcription_corrections: In (iv) the image reads 'Conditions équivalentes sur A ∈ F' (a slip for A ⊂ F); the machine transcription gives ⊂.
Struck text after (iv): 'On dira alors que A est une partie [supp-fermée] de F, ou un "F-support"'.
In (vi) the struck phrase is closer to 'a une application de ℘(F) ... anti' with 'anti' inserted above 'iso.'; it reads 'induit une anti-iso. d'ens. ordonnés Σ⁰_F → Σ⁰_F' rather than 'anti bij.'.
Last line: '∁A = cosupp. A' preceded by 'On pose aussi, si A est un support'.
